name: Facial contouring surgery for first impressions

image.caption: Facial contouring surgery for first impressions

lead: Facial contouring surgery is a group of operations that reshape the facial skeleton or add implants to change the outline of the face. Common procedures include mandibular angle reduction, malar (cheekbone) reduction, genioplasty on the chin and augmentation with implants or bone cement.

The appearance payoff is a slimmer, more defined or more balanced face. It is especially popular in East Asia, where a square lower face and prominent cheekbones are frequent reasons patients seek surgery, and surgical literature describes the techniques in detail.

paras: Surgeons plan the operation from examination and imaging, often with digital planning, then reduce, reposition or augment bone through incisions commonly made inside the mouth. Newer work uses 3D planning and robot-assisted techniques. Swelling settles over weeks to months.

Reported concerns include bleeding, asymmetry, nerve injury, under- or over-correction and the need for revision. A review of court cases describes aesthetic surgery lawsuits being lost over inadequate informed consent. Patients are generally seen by plastic or maxillofacial surgeons who discuss the risks.

angle.text: Surgeons alter the skeleton or add implants so the visible outline of the face changes. Patients choose procedures according to which feature they want narrowed, projected or balanced.

lead: Facial contouring surgery covers operations that reshape the facial skeleton or add implants to alter the face's silhouette. Reviews in the plastic surgery literature describe mandibular angle reduction, malar reduction and genioplasty as the most common procedures, performed alone or alongside orthognathic surgery [1][2].

How it helps looks: reducing a prominent jaw angle or cheekbone narrows the face, while chin and forehead work change proportion. A Korean study of lower-face surgery found that prominent mandibles and a squared contour are considered unattractive in several Asian countries, and that leaving the chin unaltered was a major reason for dissatisfaction after mandible reduction [3]. The procedures are also discussed in terms of first impressions, since the face's outline is among the first things seen.
Research consists mainly of surgical technique reports and reviews, including work on digital planning, augmented reality and robot assistance [4][5].
infobox: Mandibular angle reduction, malar reduction, genioplasty, implants

paras: A review of facial contouring in Asians describes mandibular angle reduction, malar reduction, genioplasty and body contouring as independent or ancillary procedures during orthognathic surgery, with many osteotomy designs developed to improve outcomes and limit complications [1]. A narrative review of mandibular angle osteotomy states that techniques differ mainly in the starting point, endpoint and trajectory of the osteotomy line [2]. An older review notes that Asian patients, particularly women, tend to prefer a more delicate and feminine facial shape and that reduction malarplasty and mandibular angleplasty are the common operations [6].

Authors from one centre report that digital pre-operative design reduces operating time and bleeding, that augmented reality improves surgeons' perception, and that robot-assisted surgery has strong application prospects [4]. A randomised controlled trial of a robot developed by the same group reports interim results [5]. Alloplastic implants for facial contouring have been described since at least the early 1990s [7].

Reviews discuss complication risk as a driver of technique development [1]. An analysis of aesthetic-surgery court precedents in Korea between 1995 and 2015 found that doctors lose a growing number of lawsuits when informed consent cannot be proved [8].

Evidence consists of narrative reviews, case series and a few randomised trials of technique and technology, such as a randomised trial of robot-assisted facial bone contouring [5]. A Korean review of unsatisfactory mandible-reduction cases highlighted the importance of the chin to the result [3]. Few studies examine whether surgery changes first impressions or career outcomes.

timeline.event: Article describes alloplastic implants as 'surgery of the fourth plane' for facial contouring [7].
Study on narrowing genioplasty for slim lower-face contour published [3].
Reviews and a randomised trial on digital and robot-assisted facial bone contouring published [4][5].
